Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Body, health & movement

crash verb and noun

a collision

also collision, collide, crash into

classical

collīdō, collīdere, collīsī, collīsum

verb, third conjugation, transitive

dash or strike things together

To describe objects colliding, use the passive collīdī, with inter sē when appropriate. For toy cars the vehicle nouns have modern applications; the example sentence is our composed description, not an ancient quotation.

Other words

  • collīsiō, collīsiōnis f. — collision

    noun, third declension · post-classical · M-O s.v. collision (auto), citing Traupman; Traupman 216

    Morgan–Owens records the automobile application, citing Traupman.

  • collīsus, collīsūs m. — collision

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. collision (auto), with a Vatican Lexicon reference

Examples

  • Autoraedae inter sē collīduntur.

    The cars crash into each other.composed

See also crash, collapse.

SourcesLewis & Short: collido (dictionary transcription) · Morgan–Owens: collision (auto)

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
